steps.say: A main clause makes sense on its own.
Some clauses cannot stand alone. They start with words like when, because, although, if, until and while.
A complex sentence joins a main clause to one of these clauses.
steps.show: When the bell rang, the children ran outside.

steps.say: Each joining word has a job. Because gives a reason, although shows a contrast and until shows a time limit.
If the joining clause comes first, put a comma before the main clause.
steps.show: If you are ready, we can go. We can go if you are ready.

options.why: Although shows a contrast. It does not fit here.
Unless means if not. It does not fit here.

hints: You need a word that means up to the time when.
Read the sentence with each word.
check.explanation: Until means up to the time when. We waited until the rain stopped.

check.prompt: Which sentence is a complex sentence?

options.text: Although it was late, we kept playing.

hints: A complex sentence has a clause that cannot stand alone.
Look for a joining word like although or when.
Which sentence has a comma between two clauses?
check.explanation: Although it was late cannot stand alone. It is joined to the main clause we kept playing.
